classify_evidences.text: Here, we identified novel genes, STM-like and KNAT2-like1, and new expression patterns that have emerged in the FIM and receptacle, contributing to the evolution of inferior ovaries in cucumber.

Our cell lineage analysis revealed that the prolonged activity of the floral intercalary meristem (FIM) at the base of the floral organs in cucumber, leads to rapid growth of the receptacle, which results in inferior ovary formation.

Our findings elucidate molecular mechanisms underlying inferior ovary development and highlight the importance of duplicated TFs in species diversification, adaptive genetic variation and the emergence of novel complex traits.
For example, duplication events involving genes, such as MADS, SEU and YABBY, may have contributed to the evolution of the GRN for fruit development9.
in the FIM and receptacle, leading to the evolutionary innovation of an inferior ovary in the cucurbits.

in the FIM and receptacle, leading to the evolutionary innovation of an inferior ovary in the cucurbits.

To dissect the underlying gene expression network driving the development of the inferior ovary of cucumber, we sampled floral buds at various stages, including S1–S8, and ovaries at 0 days post anthesis (DPA) for spatial transcriptomic analysis.
These data enabled us to identify distinct cell types involved in female flower and inferior ovary development.

In addition, we dissected the gene regulatory networks (GRNs) responsible for the rapid growth of the receptacle and identified key genes involved in these processes, including a duplicated class I KNOTTED-like homeobox (KNOX) transcription factor (TF), the knockout of which results in bisexual flowers with superior ovaries similar to those of tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.).
